title: A check's behaviour is described only by its own failure message
context: By 2026-09-27 check-workflow.js held about thirty rules and had changed twenty times in ten days, nearly once per Change. Each rule's behaviour was written three times: in the code, in WORKFLOW.md, and as a list in the delivery-workflow Feature. In blueprint-contract-guardrails a rule written from the WORKFLOW prose contradicted the gate-branch-state check, and two review rounds passed before a browser read exposed it.
decision: What a mechanical check enforces is stated once, in the message it prints when it fails, and in its test. WORKFLOW.md names the command a step runs, not the rules that command applies, and Feature pages do not list checks. A check whose only purpose is to require or forbid wording in another document is removed rather than kept in step with it.

alternatives.option: Keep the list in WORKFLOW.md and drop only the Feature's copy
alternatives.reason: It halves the copies but keeps the one that contradicted the code this time; the prose and the code would still drift apart silently.

alternatives.option: Generate the WORKFLOW list from the checks
alternatives.reason: A generator and its drift test are more machinery to guard a list nobody needs before running the command, whose failures already say what is wrong.

consequences: A reader of WORKFLOW.md learns what a gate checks by running it or reading its failure messages, not from the contract.
Adding a check means writing a failure message a reader can act on, since that message is its only description.
